correctness.rationale: In characteristic two, d(q^2)=0, so the Jacobian ideal is exactly the four squarefree cubic monomials whose reduced zero set is the six tetrahedron edges. Modulo this ideal, the quartic equation is q^2. Restricting q to each edge gives a binary quadratic A s^2+Bst+C t^2; over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two it has two distinct nonendpoint roots exactly when A,B,C are all nonzero. Across all six edges this is exactly the nonvanishing of the four a_i and six b_ij. At each resulting point q is a local parameter along the edge and the surface equation becomes uv+w^2, an A1 node. The localized Jacobian scheme is (u,v,w^2), length 2, so total length is 24. The packaged exact checker independently verifies the derivative structure and a 12-point F4 witness.
